sections.h2: Where is Grady County and which towns sit inside it?
sections.html:
Grady County lies along Georgia's southern border with Florida. Cairo holds the courthouse and is the biggest city. Its charter dates to August 17, 1905, when the legislature carved it out of Decatur and Thomas counties; the name honors Henry W. Grady, an orator and newspaper editor in Atlanta (Wikipedia).

The county spans 460 square miles, 455 of them land. Most of it drains to the upper Ochlockonee River, the northwest corner reaches the Flint River basin, and part of the Red Hills Region falls inside the line. Mitchell County borders it on the north, Thomas on the east and Decatur on the west, while the Florida counties of Leon and Gadsden form the southern edge.

Only Cairo and Whigham are incorporated. Calvary counts as a census-designated place, while Beachton and Spence are unincorporated crossroads communities. Grady County Schools operates six public schools, including Cairo High School. Real property anywhere in the county goes onto one county digest, and a city can levy its own tax too, so check each line of a bill before you agree on a price.

sections.h2: How many people and homes does Grady County have?
sections.html:
Census Bureau counts show 26,236 people in 2020 and 26,590 in the July 2025 estimate, a 1.4% increase. Older residents are a large group: 21.2% are 65 or over, so age-based exemptions come up often when owners plan a move.

QuickFacts puts 19.5% of residents below the poverty line, and an owner who has fallen behind is better off getting a payoff number from the commissioner before choosing how to sell (QuickFacts).

sections.h2: Which Grady County offices handle valuation and billing?
sections.html:
Collection and valuation sit in separate offices. The commissioner bills tax on real and personal property, motor vehicles, mobile homes and timber. Valuation, returns and the conservation or agricultural applications belong to the Tax Assessor office, which the county says is led by a chief appraiser.

  • Tax commissioner, per the qPublic site: 114 1st Street NE, Cairo, GA 39828, property phone 229-377-3322, open from 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM Monday to Thursday and shut on Fridays.
  • County service pages for the commissioner and the assessor: 33 17th Avenue NW, Cairo, GA 39827, with eight-to-five weekday hours.
  • Parcel lookup: the commissioner's qPublic site offers a search of every property in the county.

The two pages disagree on address and hours. Phone 229-377-3322 before you go in person, and ask which counter takes the payment you plan to bring. Updates appear on the county's commissioner page and assessor page.

sections.h2: How does a Grady County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
Assessed value in Georgia is 40% of the January 1 fair market value, and each year the assessors mail a notice showing both. An owner who disagrees writes to the Board of Tax Assessors, and the envelope must carry a postmark within 45 days of the notice's mailing date. The written appeal names a path: the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator, using state form PT-311A (Georgia Department of Revenue FAQ).

Grady County's 2024 cycle ran late. A delayed revaluation meant assessment notices were mailed in September, and the county warned that appeal windows would close October 28 for some owners and October 31 for others. It added that the digest would reach the tax commissioner behind schedule, that the rate could not be set until December, and that commissioners expected a significant decrease in the mill rate after the revaluation (county notice).

A title company working out a payoff may ask which value your bill rests on, so keep the notice and any appeal letter in your closing file.

sections.h2: What due date will a Grady County bill show?
sections.html:
Georgia's default deadline is December 20, but the Department of Revenue's Grady facts page says local government may substitute December 1 or November 15, or split the bill into installments. Look at the date printed on your bill. Interest does not start until 60 days after the postmark on the bill, and penalties can be added to unpaid sums later (Grady County property tax facts).

Ask the commissioner for the penalty and interest figures on any overdue parcel instead of guessing. A few fixed points in the calendar apply here as well:

  • Returns for property owned on January 1 are accepted from January 1 to April 1.
  • A mobile home in the county on January 1 must be returned for tax by April 1, along with the location permit.
  • Requests for a refund of wrongly assessed tax must begin within three years of payment.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special assessments can Grady County owners claim?
sections.html:
Homestead filing can happen any time after you move in, with April 1 as the cutoff for the first year of the exemption. The assessor's page cites code section 48-5-44, and the state treats skipping the filing as giving up the exemption. The standard state deduction is $2,000 from assessed value. The Department's Grady facts page reports no local homestead amounts beyond that, but it carries a 2016 date, so ask the assessor about newer ones.

In January 2025 the county posted a notice that commissioners planned to opt out of the statewide adjusted base year homestead exemption, with public hearings on February 17 and 18, 2025. Ask the assessor what that means for your home before you promise a buyer a frozen value.

  • Conservation use or preferential agricultural assessment: applications run from January 1 to April 1.
  • Freeport exemption for commercial and industrial inventory: applies only where local voters adopted it, filed with the assessors on the return schedule.
  • A buyer must file in their own name, because an exemption does not pass with the deed.

sections.h2: What did the county's 2026 millage notice say?
sections.html:
In November 2026 the county posted a notice saying the Board of Commissioners had tentatively set a rate that would raise property tax revenue by 4.72 percent. The tentative county rate was 12.64 mills, up .57 mills, against a no-increase rate of no more than 12.070 mills, and three hearings were set for that month at 33 17th Avenue NW in Cairo (county notice).

That rate covers the county levy only. School and city rates are set separately, and the final figures appear on the bill itself. Ask the commissioner's office for adopted rates when you need a payoff figure.

sections.h2: How should a Grady County seller handle tax at closing?
sections.html:
Ownership on January 1 fixes liability for that year. The Department of Revenue explains that even a January 2 sale leaves the January 1 owner responsible, with no partial-year refund. The contract and the settlement statement therefore split the bill, and they should show who pays what.

  • Phone the commissioner for the amount owed on the parcel this year and any past year.
  • Mention any open appeal to the closing agent so a changed bill can be handled.
  • Hand the closing agent the payoff figure and the office that receives the payment.
  • Notify the office when a homestead exemption no longer applies after you leave.

Even a buyer paying cash for a house as-is takes the parcel with its tax history, so arrears belong on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Grady County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Visit the tax commissioner's office in Cairo. The commissioner's own page lists 114 1st Street NE, open 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM Monday to Thursday, while the county service page gives 33 17th Avenue NW with eight-to-five weekday hours. Phone 229-377-3322 first to confirm the right counter.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Grady County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the mailing date of the notice. The written appeal must be postmarked inside that period and sent to the Board of Tax Assessors on state form PT-311A, naming the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or arbitration.

faqs.q: Does Grady County offer its own homestead exemptions?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue's county facts page, dated 2016, lists none beyond the statewide ones. A 2025 county notice about opting out of the adjusted base year exemption means you should ask the assessor which freeze rules cover your home today.

faqs.q: If I close a Grady County sale in March, who owes that year's tax?
faqs.a: Whoever owned on January 1. State law offers no partial-year refund, so the contract and settlement statement decide the split. Confirm the figure with the tax commissioner before closing.

faqs.q: Is a refund possible for Grady County tax paid in error?
faqs.a: Yes, for tax that was erroneously or illegally assessed and collected. Put the request in writing within three years of the payment. If an appeal is pending, the refund is processed automatically once the final taxable value is set.
